text: The next morning. <break time="0.8s" /> Helen went to Hagenzeele Third. <break time="0.8s" /> A cemetery raised above the road. <break time="0.8s" /> Where row after row of black crosses. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood in the raw, unfinished ground. <break time="0.8s" /> The place already held twenty one thousand dead. <break time="0.8s" /> And as she stared at the endless crosses. <break time="0.8s" /> She realized. <break time="0.8s" /> That she had no idea. <break time="0.8s" /> How to find Michael among them. <break time="0.8s" /> She wandered helplessly. <break time="0.8s" /> To the left and to the right among the rows. <break time="0.8s" /> Wondering by what guidance. <break time="0.8s" /> She would ever find her own. <break time="0.8s" /> Then she noticed a man kneeling. <break time="0.8s" /> Behind a line of headstones. <break time="0.8s" /> Firming a young plant. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the soft earth. <break time="0.8s" /> And she went toward him. <break time="0.8s" /> To ask for help. <break time="0.8s" /> When she came near the man rose from his work among the graves. <break time="0.8s" /> And asked her quietly. <break time="0.8s" /> Who are you looking for. <break time="0.8s" /> Lieutenant Michael Turrell, my nephew. <break time="0.8s" /> Helen answered slowly and word for word. <break time="0.8s" /> Exactly as she had said it countless times. <break time="0.8s" /> Throughout her life. <break time="0.8s" /> The man looked at her. <break time="0.8s" /> With infinite compassion. <break time="0.8s" /> And said. <break time="0.8s" /> Come with me. <break time="0.8s" /> And I will show you. <break time="0.8s" /> Where your son lies. <break time="0.8s" /> When Helen left the cemetery. <break time="0.8s" /> She looked back. <break time="0.8s" /> And saw the man. <break time="0.8s" /> Still bending over his young plants. <break time="0.8s" /> And she went away. <break time="0.8s" /> Supposing him to be the gardener.
